sources.headline: Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats
sources.text: Seven passenger planes across Europe, two of which departed from the UK, have been inspected following a series of suspected bomb threats.Two Ryanair flights, one originating from Dublin and the other from Lisbon, were searched after landing in Rome following anonymous tips but no explosives were found, sources at the city's Fiumicino airport told the BBC. The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air Force until landing. Authorities have also searched planes in Poland, Spain and Bulgaria. While officially there is no link between them, authorities from various countries will be co-operating to assess whether this was a co-ordinated attack, designed to disrupt airspace.The UK government described today's incidents as "malicious hoax threats".In a statement it said it had "one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we've seen today". Aviation security expert Paul Mason said bomb threats on passenger planes "don't happen that frequently", which made the latest incidents "unusual"."It sounds like they've been made in a credible manner across a broad range of airlines," Mason told BBC Radio 5 Live. "That would suggest to me that it's been a very deliberate act by a typical actor rather than a load of coincidental, malicious calls."He said "there are a lot of processes" that the onboard crew and people on the ground must go through "to validate the credibility of the threat".A flight may be asked to divert if the credibility of a threat "is of a certain level", Mason added, and in some cases the onboard crew may not even be advised on what the ground operators were dealing with.In Rome, sources at Fiumicino airport told the BBC police bomb disposal experts carried out standard security protocols to ensure the safety of all passengers and crew.Inspections of the passengers, luggage, and the aircraft yielded negative results, and the alert has since been cleared.One plane which landed in Murcia, southern Spain - a Ryanair flight coming from Manchester - was also found not to have any explosives on board, Spanish authorities said.One passenger later said she was unaware of the bomb threat until after the plane landed."We weren't told anything during the flight," Sarah told BBC Radio 5 Live. "The plane stopped quite suddenly and then we were kept on the runway for around 30 minutes.""Then the fire engines turned up, the bomb squad turned up and we were asked to evacuate," she continues.Sarah said the plane had not been on the ground a minute before it was "surrounded by fire engines and police and a bomb squad". All the passengers were then escorted by police, leaving all their belongings."We were only later told that it was an actual threat, a bomb threat to the plane itself," she added.Two flights heading to Warsaw were also affected, including one from London Heathrow.The Heathrow flight was originally meant to land at the Polish capital's main airport, Chopin, but was diverted instead to the smaller Modlin airport, briefly forcing its closure. A Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen to Warsaw-Chopin landed as planned.In a separate development, a bomb alert triggered the evacuation of 1,537 passengers and crew from an Israel-bound cruise ship in Greece, media reports from both countries say.Initial checks of the Panama-flagged Crown Iris vessel currently docked at a port on the Aegean island of Syros found no explosives, they said citing the Greek Coast Guard. A second inspection is expected shortly. Tuesday's aircraft incidents come a day after a Wizz Air flight from London Luton made an emergency landing in Budapest, escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet, after a bomb threat.Wizz Air said later that security checks had been made and nothing was found.BBC Verify has consulted aviation safety experts about what happens on board a plane when a bomb threat is issued.Marco Chan, a former pilot for Cathay Pacific Airways and Hong Kong Airlines who is now a senior lecturer in aviation operations at Kingston University, said a bomb threat is considered "genuine until it is resolved, even though most turn out to be hoaxes".Chan said crews will "quietly search" toilets, galleys and storage areas and will not touch a suspicious item unless it has to be taken to an area on the aircraft designated as the least risky bomb location.The aircraft's captain will have multiple factors to assess, according to former airline pilot Terry Tozer, an aviation safety commentator. He said these include what facilities are available at the airport they are being diverted to and how the plane can continue onwards should it turn out to be a false threat.Chan added that once on the ground, the plane is generally "taken to an isolated stand, passengers are disembarked, and police and bomb disposal teams search it".

sources.headline: Seven reported bomb threats against European flights confirmed as false alarms – as it happened
sources.text:
From 7h agoAll reported bomb threats against European flightsBringing it all together, seven bomb threats have now been reported in total:
LOT Polish Airlines flight from London Heathrow, UK to Warsaw Okęcie, diverted to Warsaw Modlin, Poland (10:33, 10:58, 12:00, 13:57).
SAS flight from Copenhagen, Denmark to Warsaw Okęcie (11:33, 12:59).
Ryanair flight from Manchester, UK to Murcia, Spain (12:44, 13:44)
Ryanair flight from Lisbon, Portugal to Rome, Italy (15:02)
Ryanair flight from Dublin, Ireland to Rome, Italy
WizzAir flight from Bergamo, Italy to Sofia, Bulgaria (15:41)
Ryanair flight from Dublin, Ireland to Sofia, Bulgaria
All seven have been confirmed to be false alarms.Key events3h agoClosing summary4h agoBomb threat prompts checks on Israel-bound cruise ship in Greek port4h agoCzech public media workers strike over government plan to overhaul funding7h agoAll reported bomb threats against European flights7h agoBulgaria confirms bomb threats against flights from Bergamo, Dublin, not Israel8h agoTwo false bomb threats reported on Italy-bound Ryanair flights8h agoSecurity guarantees, Ukraine reconstructions, energy and Black Sea truce to be discussed in Abu Dhabi, Zelenskyy says8h agoEurope remains 'crucial' for ending the war in Ukraine, Zelenskyy says, as he confirms Abu Dhabi talks8h agoMerz declares Germany will keep supporting Ukraine as he warns about Russia's attacks, impact of Black Sea strikes on food security9h agoPolish authorities call off bomb alert on London flight9h agoSpanish police rules out presence of explosives on Ryanair flight to Murcia9h agoSwedish centrist Thand Ringqvist rejected as prime minister as search for new government continues9h agoFlights from London, Copenhagen, Manchester and Israel affected by bomb threats10h agoEU to host talks on Ukraine with EU, US, Nato, World Bank on Wednesday11h agoWarsaw Modlin airport resumes operations after bomb threat reported on London flight11h agoBerlin talks with Merz to focus on diplomacy, air defence, energy, Zelenskyy says11h agoMerz hosts Lithuania's Nausėda ahead of Zelenskyy talks11h agoKremlin confirms Abu Dhabi talks with US, Ukraine next week12h agoWarsaw Modlin airport closed after bomb threat reported on London flight12h agoRussian attacks on Ukraine on US election day 'telling,' Zelenskyy says13h agoMorning opening: Zelenskyy to make unexpected visit to Berlin for talks with MerzClosing summary
At least seven flights and a cruise ship in Europe received bomb threats, causing disruption at airports although ⁠no devices were discovered. At least two flights to Warsaw, two to Sofia, two to Rome and one to Murcia airport in Spain were subjected to the threats on Tuesday and another flight to Sofia had been threatened a day earlier. ⁠
An airport in Warsaw was briefly ⁠shut and the Italian Air Force ​accompanied one of the flights to Rome, while an Israel-bound cruise ship was searched for bombs in Greece.
Authorities diverted a LOT flight from London that was meant to land at Warsaw’s Chopin airport to nearby Modlin airport, which was closed and then reopened ​after the plane was searched and no device was found. Another Warsaw-bound flight, an ‌SAS flight from Copenhagen, landed at Chopin as ‌scheduled. Chopin airport said no device was found and the airport remained operational.
Bomb threats were made against planes traveling from Milan/Bergamo and Dublin ‌to Sofia, Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in a statement to Reuters. Both landed safely and no explosive devices were found on inspection.
The Bergamo flight was operated by Wizz Air and was carrying 176 passengers, the statement said. The Dublin flight, operated by Ryanair, had 186 passengers on board. Bulgarian news agency BTA had earlier quoted an interior ministry official as saying a flight from Israel had been affected, but authorities later said this was not the case.
In Murcia in southeastern ‌Spain, parts of an airport were cordoned off after a bomb threat was reported on a Ryanair flight from Manchester. Officials said the report proved to be a hoax, and the airport resumed normal operations after authorities found no explosives on board.
Two other Ryanair flights - one from Lisbon and another from Dublin - were searched at Rome’s Fiumicino airport following bomb threats, said a source from airport operator ADR. The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air Force until it landed. The alert was cleared and the airport continued to operate as usual with no effects on other flights, the person said.
An explosives detection dog and a diver searched the Panama-flagged Crown Iris cruise ship on the Greek island of Syros after an unknown person said an explosive device had ⁠been attached to the boat’s hull, authorities said. Initial checks found no explosive device with coast guard specialists expected to carry ​out further inspections before the ship could resume its voyage.
Meanwhile, Czech public media workers went on a one-day strike to protest a government plan to overhaul how public broadcasters are funded. The legislation, led by populist billionaire turned prime minister Andrej Babiš, has been criticised as threatening the independence of the media organisations.
Russia bombarded Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in waves on ⁠Tuesday, knocking out power to swathes of the country with dozens of missiles and hundreds of drones, a week before US-brokered peace talks were due to resume.
At a ​press conference in Berlin with German chancellor Friedrich Merz, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attack showed that ‌Moscow was intent on killing people instead of building ‌on the humanitarian ceasefire in and around Oleshky.
Merz warned that the outcome of the war in Ukraine “will determine European security for a long time to come.” He said Germany will be coordinating with France and the UK, and will host a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin later this month.
The European Commission will host ⁠a meeting regarding Ukraine with representatives ⁠from the ⁠United ​States, Ukraine and its key European allies on Wednesday, Commission ⁠spokesperson Paula Pinho said. “So tomorrow the European ⁠Commission will host a ​meeting with representatives ‌from Ukraine, ‌from the United States, France, Germany, ‌the UK, Nato and the World Bank and this meeting will build on earlier talks that took place ‌in Miami,” Pinho told reporters in Brussels.
Bomb threat prompts checks on Israel-bound cruise ship in Greek portA bomb threat to an ⁠Israel-bound cruise ship prompted a security operation at the ⁠Greek island port of ⁠Syros after an unknown person claimed ⁠an explosive device had been attached to its hull, Greek authorities said.The ⁠Panama-flagged Crown Iris was due ​to sail ‌to Haifa carrying ‌940 passengers and 597 crew ‌members when the threat was received, Reuters reported.Coast guard personnel assisted by an explosives detection dog and a private diver searched the vessel, while ‌a special coast guard unit was deployed to the scene.Initial ​checks found no explosive device. Coast guard specialists are expected to arrive at 9.30pm (7.30pm GMT) ⁠to carry out further inspections before the ​ship ​can resume its voyage.Czech public media workers strike over government plan to overhaul fundingHere are some images from earlier today as Czech public media workers went on a one-day strike to protest a government plan to overhaul how public broadcasters are funded.The legislation, led by populist billionaire turned prime minister Andrej Babiš, has been criticised as threatening the independence of the media organisations. The plan led to street protests in Prague last month.Employees of Czech Television holding a banner reading 'Strike' march in front of the broadcaster's headquarters in Prague, Czechia. Photograph: Martin Divíšek/EPAUnder the plan, the country’s public radio and television would be financed from the state budget, not from an existing system of regular fees from individuals, households and businesses. The media would receive about 15% less money than they do now, which could likely lead to staff layoffs, limited production and program cancellations.Demonstrators gather at Wenceslas Square in Prague, Czechia, 03 November 2026, during a nationwide walkout by staff of public service broadcasters Czech Television and Czech Radio. Photograph: Martin Divíšek/EPACritics say the overhaul would give the ruling three-party coalition the means to take control of the media, similar to what populist governments did in Slovakia under prime minister Robert Fico and in Hungary before former prime minister Viktor Orbán was ousted from power in April.Michal Kubal, chief news editor at Czech Television, said the strike today is unprecedented in the history of Czech public service media.Public gathering in support of Czech Television employees during a strike by Czech public television and radio workers against government plans to cut financing and move funding to the state budget. Photograph: Eva K

Bomb threats against European airlines force Warsaw airport closure, affect several flights

Bomb threats targeted at least 10 European airlines on Tuesday, forcing the temporary closure of a Warsaw airport and affecting at least four Ryanair flights. No explosives were found after the planes all took off and landed safely in different European cities. 

Issued on: 03/11/2026 - 16:41
Modified: 03/11/2026 - 20:34

  3 min
Reading time
Share
By:
FRANCE 24
No explosives were found, despite extensive searches on the ground after the planes all took off and landed safely in different European cities just several hours apart. © Attila Kisbenedek, AFP

About 10 European flights were targeted by bomb threats on Tuesday, forcing the brief closure of a Warsaw airport and the scrambling of air force planes in Rome, authorities said.

No explosives were found, despite extensive searches on the ground after the planes all took off and landed safely in different European cities just several hours apart. 

Matthew Borie of Osprey Flight Solutions, which advises airlines on flight threats, laid out several hypotheses for the as-yet unexplained incidents: A single threat triggers copycat incidents; an individual or a group makes multiple threats; or operations of “hybrid warfare” by state actors or their supporters. 

Such threats were “not a new phenomenon” and come at a time of increased geopolitical tensions and signs of “disruption”, like attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems, drone incursions in Europe and mysterious triggers to alert apps — even as authorities have warned that hybrid threats abound.

The focus on Europe means "there could be a Russian angle," said Borie, the company's co-founder and chief intelligence officer. "We need to keep in mind, though, that Iranian hybrid warfare is just as active in certain pockets of Europe as well.”

His message for travellers? “Don't be alarmed,” he said, noting “coordinated response mechanisms” by national authorities — including, at times, the deployment of NATO fighter jets to escort such planes.

Irish budget carrier Ryanair appeared to be the worst hit, with four of its flights to different destinations being targeted.

London's Metropolitan police confirmed it "was made aware of threats ... against four aircraft due to depart from or arrive at Heathrow Airport" Tuesday, one of Europe's busiest air hubs.

It gave no further details, but also said there was a further warning about a flight at Manchester Airport.

Following checks "no security issues were identified", the Met police added.

Bomb-disposal robot and drone with explosives discovered at Germany's Leipzig airport
Cover image: © France 24
01:19

Two bomb warnings targeted planes heading to the Polish capital Warsaw, including an SAS Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen and one from Heathrow operated by Polish airline LOT, Polish airport authorities said.

Aena, the Spanish airport operator, confirmed an emergency protocol was activated "due to a bomb alert" on a Ryanair flight which landed at 10:30am (0930 GMT) from Manchester at Murcia in southeastern Spain. The plane arrived without problems.

Other Ryanair flights from Lisbon to Rome, Dublin to Rome, and Dublin to the Bulgarian capital of Sofia also received warnings.

Italian air force jets were scrambled to escort Ryanair flight FR9611 from Dublin as it landed at Rome-Fiumicino at 10:45am (0945 GMT), Rome Airport said in a statement.

Anti-bomb procedures were also put in place when an earlier Ryanair flight arrived at 9:40am (0840 GMT) at the airport. "Checks on passengers, luggage and the plane were all negative and the alert was lifted," the statement added.

A Wizz Air flight from Bergamo, Italy, was inspected after landing at 0910 GMT in the Bulgarian capital Sofia following an alert, a Bulgarian interior ministry spokesperson told AFP.

The incidents all come after fighter jets were scrambled on Monday when a Wizz Air flight from London's Luton airport to Sofia was diverted following a bomb threat and forced to make an emergency stop in Budapest.

Read moreGermany blames Russia for Leipzig airport drone attack, orders Russian consulate closed

Airport briefly shut

Scandinavian Airlines said it could "confirm that a threat has been made against flight SK751 between Copenhagen and Warsaw" but the plane landed Tuesday without any problem.

It arrived at Warsaw's Chopin airport, which closed one runway as the plane underwent a security inspection, but no explosives were found.

The LOT flight, which had also been scheduled to arrive at Chopin, was diverted to the Polish capital's other airport, Warsaw Modlin.

Authorities closed that airport following the alert, but the Boeing 737 MAX also landed safely. "Nothing was found," Modlin airport spokesman Adam Szablowski told AFP.

Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said on Facebook that on Monday NATO's air defence alert service had issued an alert for a Wizz Air flight from London's Luton.

"The Hungarian Defence Forces' Gripen fighter jets took to the air within minutes and ensured the safe landing of the passenger aircraft in Budapest," he said.

(FRANCE 24 with AFP and AP)

sources.headline: Hoax bomb threats target four European flights as scares spread across the continent
sources.text:
Published on 3 November 2026 - 16:45 GMT+1•Updated
17:01
Four passenger flights heading to Poland, Spain and Bulgaria were the target of bomb threats on Tuesday. All of them landed safely and no explosives were found, authorities said.
Two of the threats involved flights heading for Warsaw. The first was SAS Scandinavian Airlines flight SK751 from Copenhagen, which landed normally at the Polish capital’s main Chopin airport. One runway there was closed while the aircraft was searched.
“The aircraft landed normally in Warsaw and the passengers have disembarked,” the Scandinavian carrier said after confirming a threat had been made against the flight.
The second was a LOT Polish Airlines Boeing 737 MAX flying from London Heathrow. It had been due at Chopin but was diverted to Warsaw Modlin, the city’s second airport, which was closed after the alert.
“The passengers were evacuated and the plane underwent security checks. Nothing was found,” Modlin spokesman Adam Szablowski told AFP, adding that the airport had since reopened and was operating normally.
In Spain, airport operator Aena activated an emergency protocol “due to a bomb alert” on a Ryanair flight from Manchester, in northwest England, to Murcia in the country’s southeast. The plane landed without incident, and the emergency plan was stood down after the Civil Guard had checked the aircraft.
The fourth flight was a Wizz Air service from Bergamo in northern Italy. It was inspected after landing in the Bulgarian capital, Sofia, at 10:10 CET, according to a spokesperson for Bulgaria’s interior ministry.
The threats came a day after NATO’s air defence alert service raised the alarm over another Wizz Air flight, which was flying from London Luton to Sofia. That plane was diverted and made an emergency landing in Budapest.
“The Hungarian Defence Forces’ Gripen fighter jets took to the air within minutes and ensured the safe landing of the passenger aircraft in Budapest,” Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said on Facebook.
On Sunday, an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna was also rerouted to Bulgaria after a bomb threat. Nothing was found on board.

Published: 3:04am, 4 Nov 2026

At least seven flights and a cruise ⁠ship in Europe received bomb threats on ⁠Tuesday, causing disruption at airports although no devices were discovered.

At least ⁠two flights to Warsaw, two to Sofia, two to Rome and one to Murcia airport in Spain were subjected to the threats on Tuesday, and another flight to Sofia had been threatened a day earlier.

An airport in Warsaw was briefly shut, and the Italian Air Force accompanied one of the flights to Rome while an Israel-bound cruise ship was searched for bombs in Greece.

There was no claim of responsibility and officials did ‌not attribute blame. None of the affected airlines responded to Reuters’ requests for comment.

Rhys Jones, Analysis Output Manager at aviation risk advisory firm Osprey Flight Solutions, said that seven confirmed bomb threats in a single day affecting flights was exceptional.

“The lack of clear target state, airline, or route indicates that general disruption to aviation operations is the aim,” Jones said.

An SAS aircraft flying from Copenhagen lands at Warsaw Chopin Airport in Poland on Tuesday, after receiving a bomb threat. Photo: Piotr Bozyk via Reuters

Authorities diverted a LOT flight from London that was meant to land at Warsaw’s Chopin airport to nearby Modlin airport, which was closed and then reopened after the plane was searched and no device was found.

Another Warsaw-bound flight, an SAS flight from Copenhagen, landed at Chopin as scheduled. Chopin airport said ⁠no device was found and the airport remained operational.

Bomb threats were made against planes travelling from Milan/Bergamo and Dublin to Sofia, Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in ‌a statement. Both landed safely and no explosive devices were found on inspection.

The Bergamo flight was operated by Wizz Air and was carrying 176 passengers, the statement said. The Dublin flight, operated by Ryanair, had 186 passengers on board.

Bulgarian news agency BTA had earlier ‌quoted an Interior Ministry official as saying a flight from Israel had been affected, but authorities later said this was not the case.

A day ⁠earlier, a Wizz Air flight from London ⁠to Sofia was diverted to Budapest airport after receiving a bomb threat, Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said in a Facebook post.

In Murcia in southeastern Spain, parts of an airport were cordoned off on Tuesday after a bomb ‌threat was reported on a Ryanair flight from Manchester.

Officials said the report proved to be a hoax, and the airport resumed normal operations after authorities found no explosives on board. Ryanair declined to immediately comment.

An Israel-bound cruise ship is seen at the port of Syros, Greece, on Tuesday, after an unknown person claimed an explosive device had been attached to its hull. Photo: Reuters

Two other Ryanair flights – ‌one from ‌Lisbon and another from Dublin – were searched at Rome’s Fiumicino airport following bomb threats, said a source from airport operator ADR. The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air ‌Force until it landed.

The alert was cleared and the airport continued to operate as usual with no effects on other flights, the person said.

An explosives detection dog and a ⁠diver searched the Panama-flagged Crown Iris cruise ship on the Greek island of Syros after an unknown person said an explosive device had been attached to the boat’s hull, authorities ⁠said.

Initial checks found no explosive device with coastguard specialists expected to carry out further inspections before the ship could resume its voyage.

While no country pointed fingers over the bomb threats, they come at a time when European officials have been blaming both Russia and Iran for what they describe as “hybrid attacks” and acts ‌of sabotage. Moscow and Tehran both deny ‌any such campaign.

This week, unidentified hackers shut down fridges in supermarkets in several European countries. Some experts said hoax bomb threats could be part of a similar pattern of low-cost, deniable disruption efforts.

“From railways to the food infrastructure that you see happening with the fridges being hacked and all kinds of other operations, it does fit the narrative of Russian state actors who want to disturb Europe,” said Eric Schouten, the head of aviation security group Dyami.

sources.headline: Europe-wide bomb threats disrupt air travel
sources.text: LONDON - A string of bomb threats has disrupted passenger flights across Europe in recent days, forcing diversions, emergency landings and security sweeps, though no explosive devices have been found.Here is a list of flights affected by bomb threats in recent days.RyanairTwo Ryanair flights were searched at Rome’s Fiumicino airport following potential bomb threats on Nov 3, airport operator ADR said. A flight from Lisbon landed at 0940 CET and a flight from Dublin landed at 1030 CET, the latter escorted by the Italian Air Force until landing.Both aircraft went through security protocols including searches and bomb sweeps of the plane, luggage, passengers and crew. ADR said the alert was cleared, there was no bomb threat to the airport itself, and other flights were not affected.Murcia’s international airport activated on Nov 3 a security protocol after a bomb alert was received on a Ryanair flight from Manchester that landed at the airport, Spain’s government delegate for the Murcia region, Francisco Lucas, said on social media.All 121 people on board, 114 passengers and seven crew, disembarked and underwent security checks while security forces inspected the aircraft to determine whether the threat was real.A bomb threat was made against a Ryanair flight from Dublin to Sofia on Nov 3, Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in a statement to Reuters. The plane landed safely with 185 passengers on board, and no explosive devices were found during an inspection.Wizz AirA Wizz Air flight from Milan/Bergamo to Sofia was the target of a bomb threat on Nov 3, Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in a statement to Reuters. The plane landed safely with 176 passengers on board, and no explosive devices were found during an inspection.Another Wizz Air flight from London to Sofia diverted to Budapest on Nov 2 after a bomb threat, Hungary’s defence minister said. A Hungarian Gripen fighter was scrambled to escort the aircraft.LOT Polish AirlinesOn Nov 3, a LOT Polish Airlines flight from London made an unscheduled landing at Warsaw-Modlin airport after a bomb threat alert, a LOT spokesperson confirmed. Air operations at the airport were suspended and resumed around midday. The aircraft was checked by the relevant services, while passengers and crew waited in the arrivals hall for further decisions.SAS Scandinavian AirlinesOn Nov 3, a bomb threat was reported on an SAS flight from Copenhagen to Warsaw, which landed at Warsaw-Chopin airport and was checked, a Chopin airport spokesperson said. SAS said the aircraft landed safely and its passengers disembarked. Polish authorities said the threat was not confirmed. The airport continued operations.Austrian AirlinesEarlier, on Oct 18, an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna diverted to Sofia after a reported bomb threat while over Romania, Bulgaria’s transport ministry said.A Bulgarian air force MiG-29 escorted the Airbus A320, which landed about 30 minutes after the alert was raised, and passengers were evacuated. Austrian Airlines confirmed a threat was made and said 51 passengers and six crew were on board. No injuries were reported.The airline said the security search found no threat, and the flight later continued to Vienna with all its passengers. REUTERS
